solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soldier wearing suitable American equipment

indicators.note: the suitable word has the soldier on it, as a body wears clothes, so one goes around the other

parts.note: suitable means apt
a PARA is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: A soldier dressed in fitting American kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' makes the suitable word go round the soldier, splitting it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is a collective noun for the gear or equipment used for a task.

clue.text: Formerly a hated symbol broken in half

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for the symbol is kept once it is broken in two

parts.note: the swastika is the hated emblem of the Nazis

explanation.surface: A detested emblem of the past has been smashed into two pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: SWASTIKA halved leaves SWAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'as was' marks how something used to be, as in 'Jane Smith, as was'.

clue.text: Remarkable events in empty patch with flower springing up

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving just the outside letters
in a down entry, springing up means the flower's letters run bottom to top

parts.note: the anemone is a flower

explanation.surface: Remarkable things happen in a bare plot where a flower suddenly shoots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves PH from patch; 'springing up' turns ANEMONE into ENOMENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are striking or extraordinary occurrences, the plural of phenomenon.

clue.text: Look right up across unnamed newspaper, for example

indicators.note: the reversed look-and-right pair lies across, that is around, the trimmed newspaper
in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: unnamed means the letter N, for name, is taken away

parts.note: Le Monde is the French daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Glance up at the paper with no masthead, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper is the French daily Le Monde; 'up' reverses look-plus-right, and 'across' sets the trimmed paper between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose conduct sets an example others copy.

clue.text: The turf an object of derision for Cambridge college?

definitions.meaning: the turf is horse racing, traditionally the pastime of monarchs

definitions.text: an object of derision for Cambridge college?
definitions.meaning: a sport is a butt of jokes, and King's is a Cambridge college, so its laughing stock

explanation.surface: Racing is mocked as a figure of fun by an Oxbridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase means the plaything of King's College, Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing has long been called the pastime of royalty because monarchs bred and raced horses.

clue.text: Scarcities known to be artificial are unacceptable

indicators.note: artificial suggests something made up rather than natural, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Shortages that everyone knows are manufactured are intolerable.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARCITIES KNOWN rearranged gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that stick in one's craw are hard to swallow, so they are galling or intolerable.

clue.text: Unskilled work from son of afflicted man?

parts.note: Mac or Mc in Scottish and Irish surnames means son of
Job is the Biblical man tested by many afflictions

explanation.surface: Menial labour handed down from the offspring of a suffering man.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is a slang term for a low-paid, low-skill job with few prospects.

clue.text: Doctors succeeded saving European national leader

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe inside, so the doctors-and-succeeded letters hold the European

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, so MOS are doctors

explanation.surface: Physicians managed to rescue a continental head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt, a leader of a whole people.

clue.text: No new sort of calendar girl

indicators.note: no new means the abbreviation for new is not there

parts.note: the Julian calendar was introduced by Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: No fresh type of pin-up for the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calendar girl' reads as one phrase; it splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Julia is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Carelessly, behind sofa husband dropped proof of honesty

indicators.note: done carelessly, the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
dropped means this letter is taken out of the furniture phrase

explanation.surface: A husband carelessly let something slip down the back of the settee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes H from BEHIND SOFA, leaving BEINDSOFA, and 'Carelessly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fides, Latin for good faith, are credentials showing genuineness or sincerity.

clue.text: Trick cyclist performs in bin

definitions.meaning: a stunt riding along on the back wheel alone
a wheeled rubbish bin takes this word before bin

explanation.surface: A circus bike rider does a stunt inside a dustbin.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheelie bin is the British name for a large wheeled household rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: The stunt is lifting the front wheel, and the same word names the wheeled refuse bin.

clue.text: How unmarried couples used to live, swallowing extremely unusual hormone

indicators.note: swallowing means the phrase takes the other letters inside it

parts.words: How unmarried couples used to live
parts.note: couples living together unmarried were once said to be living in sin

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme, outer letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: The old way cohabiting couples lived takes in a very odd hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' places the ends of 'unusual' inside the old phrase 'living in sin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: Squirrel away almost months in terrible weather

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for hoarding is lost

parts.note: to squirrel away is to store

explanation.surface: A squirrel hides nuts for nearly months while the weather is foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims STORE to STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a spell of violent wind, rain or snow.

clue.text: Take fish with rod, it's plain

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: An angler's instruction: catch a fish with your rod, it's simple.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'as plain as a pikestaff'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'plain as a pikestaff' makes this wooden pole the type of something obvious.

clue.text: Provided with backing, cease being addict

indicators.note: with backing means the word for provided is read backwards

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'
to cease is to end

explanation.surface: With support, someone stops being an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with backing' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is a devotee or addict, as in a fresh-air fiend or a dope fiend.

clue.text: Port that protects marine resource?

parts.note: fish are a resource harvested from the sea
a guard is something that protects

explanation.surface: A harbour that defends the sea's stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishguard is a ferry port in Pembrokeshire, west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Welsh harbour town with ferries to Ireland.

clue.text: Academy dancers after training were very nervous

parts.note: RA stands for the Royal Academy

indicators.note: dancers after training are put through their paces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ballet students, once drilled, were full of stage fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academy' is the Royal Academy of Arts in London; 'after training' rearranges the dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have run scared is to have been frightened or panicky.

clue.text: In mock game, have decided to be inconsistent

indicators.note: in means the intended word goes inside the fake one

parts.note: cod means mock or sham, as in cod Latin
to mean to do something is to intend it, to have decided on it
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: In a pretend match, players have chosen to be erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' as an adjective meaning fake is British usage; 'In' places the intending word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something come-and-go is intermittent, appearing and vanishing irregularly.

clue.text: Meet rhyme for first clue?

definitions.meaning: the opening clue of a crossword is 1 across, which rhymes with these words

explanation.walkthrough: The first clue of a grid is usually 1 across; the answer rhymes with that label.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone unexpectedly is to come upon them by chance.

clue.text: Provincial shopping centre in the way now made to move

indicators.note: the shopping centre is placed in the other letters

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: letters made to move are rearranged into another order

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A shopping centre built across the road is now being relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to move' rearranges 'now'; 'in' sets the mall after the first letter of the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-town describes the narrow outlook of the provinces, away from the big city.

clue.text: Less threatening, to be deprived of all love

indicators.note: every occurrence of the love letter is taken away

parts.note: threatening means ominous
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: It is less menacing to lose all love.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Os go from OMINOUS, leaving MINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus means less or without, as in 'ten minus two'.

clue.text: Conspirator hanged: rope splits in two, we hear

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to steady a tent

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: something that forks divides into two branches

explanation.surface: A plotter was executed when the rope frayed and divided.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes of the 1605 Gunpowder Plot was sentenced to be hanged; FAWKES sounds like FORKS in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: He plotted to blow up Parliament and was sentenced to hang in 1606.

clue.text: I agree about returning thanks for poet

indicators.note: about means the agreement word goes around the other letters

parts.note: yes is said to agree

indicators.note: returning means the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: I concur, regarding a returned thank-you, for the verse writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' flips the British thank-you, and 'about' wraps the agreeing word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: A college year provides friendship

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A year at college gives you friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, goodwill between people or nations.

clue.text: Discharge returned bill first, producing capital

indicators.note: first means the bill comes at the front

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: returned means the discharge word is read backwards

parts.note: an arc is an electrical discharge

explanation.surface: A discharged bill sent back first yields money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ARC into CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: Chain of human descent not complete

indicators.note: neither word is complete: the letters straddle the end of one and the start of the next

explanation.surface: The line of mankind's ancestry is unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain' looks like a family chain of descent, but it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain chain down western South America.

clue.text: Part of opera, some number about sailor from foreign land

indicators.note: the opera piece goes about, that is around, the sailor

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
AB is an able-bodied seaman
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A section of opera, some musical number about a seaman from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the opera solo round the able seaman, and the number follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabian describes someone or something coming from Arabia, a land foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: Giant in forest wore odd pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are treated as a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge figure in the woods had strange trousers on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, but it is British slang for poor, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The California redwood is among the tallest trees on earth.

clue.text: Detective, modest and attractive

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
shy means modest or retiring

explanation.surface: A police inspector who is retiring and good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is British informal for good-looking.

clue.text: Proverbs about heroin that are employed by the chippy

definitions.text: that are employed by the chippy
definitions.note: a phrase standing for a plural noun: things a carpenter uses

indicators.note: the proverbs go about, that is around, the drug

parts.note: saws are old sayings or proverbs
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Wise sayings about drugs used by the fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang for a carpenter, not only a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpenters rest timber on these trestles to cut it.
